initiative.title: Run explorEDA without React at its core
initiative.summary: Feasibility read: half the library is already framework-free; a staged path leads to a React-free core with React as one renderer. A second full UI is a rewrite of about 83k lines.
initiative.next_action: Byron answers the motivation questions. Then prove stage 2: split ChartDefinition into data and a React view binding, and gate core entries against React imports.

sources.anchor: Create an initiative on what it takes to remove React as the core of the internals; scope feasibility
Line counts by folder and extension, React import counts, hook counts, ChartDefinition type

claims.statement: Find out whether React can be removed from the core of the library, and how large that is.
claims.notes: Answered in the brief: neutral core is a clear staged path; second full UI is very large.

claims.statement: About 74k of 163k non-test lines are TypeScript with no React import, including lib/, server, CLI, chart plans, and the vanilla Zustand data layer store.
ChartDefinition holds React component, settingsPanel, and icon, so core and charts/* entries import React. About 7 call sites read those fields.
Keep the existing library and demo in React; this initiative does not convert them.

human_questions: What drives this: a non-React host, new UI in SolidJS, headless rendering, or cleaner architecture?
Is an embed wrapper with React inside enough, or must the bundle have no React?
If no React, which framework first, and are charts alone in scope or the app chrome too?

shape.recommended_shape: Staged: embed wrapper, split chart contract, free the store, one neutral chart family, then decide on a second UI.
shape.first_proof: Split ChartDefinition so core and charts/* entries build without React, gated by a check.
rabbit_holes: Rewriting chart interaction (brush, hover, drag) outside React hooks
Replacing Radix, tiptap, dnd-kit, and react-grid-layout in a second framework
Keeping two chart renderers in sync

history.action: Created feasibility brief from a code scan.
history.reason: Byron asked what it takes to remove React from the internals.

intake.audience: Host developers in other frameworks; library maintainers.
